questions.question: How many people were lifted out of extreme poverty in India between 2011-12 and 2022-23, as per the World Bank?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**171 million**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• According to **World Bank** data and research papers analyzing the **Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2022-23**, India lifted approximately **171 million** people out of **extreme poverty** between **2011-12** and **2022-23**.
 
• The **extreme poverty headcount ratio** in India, measured at the international poverty line of **$2.15** per day (**2017 PPP**), declined significantly from **18.7%** in **2011-12** to **6.4%** in **2022-23**.
 
• This decline indicates a steady reduction in poverty despite the economic shocks caused by the **COVID-19 pandemic**, showcasing the resilience of the Indian economy and the effectiveness of **social safety nets**.
 
• The **World Bank** estimates suggest that **rural poverty** saw a sharper decline

questions.question: In 2025, India launched Operation SINDOOR in response to a terror attack. The operation targeted terrorist camps in which region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation SINDOOR** was a high-stakes military counter-terrorism operation launched by the **Indian Armed Forces** in the year **2025**.
 
• The operation was initiated as a direct **retaliatory response** to a major **terror attack** targeting Indian security installations, aiming to dismantle the infrastructure of terror.
 
• The primary targets of this operation were identified as **terrorist training camps** and active **launch pads** located deep within **Pakistan** and across the **Line of Control (LoC)** in **Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK)**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Pakistan and Pakistan occupied Kashmir.***
 
• This mission utilized **advanced surveillance** and **precision-strike capabilities** to ensure maximum impact on the terror modules while minimizing collateral damage.
 
• The execution of **Operation SINDOOR** reflects India’s evolved **military doctrine** of proactive deterrence, shifting from a defensive posture to one of "pre-emptive" strikes against cross-border threats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pakistan occupied Kashmir (PoK)**:
 
 
• **PoK** is a region that has been under the administrative control of **Pakistan** since the **1947** conflict, but is considered an integral part of **India** by the Indian government.
 
• It consists of two main administrative parts: **Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK)** and **Gilgit-Baltistan**.
 
• The region is strategically significant due to its **geographical location**, sharing borders with **Afghanistan** and **China**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Counter-Terror Operations**:
 
 
• **2016 Surgical Strikes**: Conducted by the **Indian Army** in response to the **Uri attack**, targeting launch pads in **PoK**.
 
• **Operation Bandar (2019)**: An aerial strike conducted by the **Indian Air Force (IAF)** on a **Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM)** camp in **Balakot**, located in the **Khyber Pakhtunkhwa** province of **Pakistan**.
 
• These operations signify the **"New India"** policy of providing a "befitting reply" to acts of **state-sponsored terrorism**.
 
 
 
• **Tactical Significance**:
 
 
• Modern operations like **Operation SINDOOR** often involve the use of **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)**, **Electronic Warfare (EW)**, and **satellite imagery** provided by **ISRO** for pinpoint accuracy.
 
• Such strikes are intended to disrupt the **logistics** and **communication channels** of extremist organizations like **Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT)** and **JeM**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geopolitical Context**: The launch of **Operation SINDOOR** in **2025** occurred amidst heightening tensions and was justified under the **Right to Self-Defense** as per **Article 51** of the **United Nations Charter**.
 
• **Line of Control (LoC)**: The **LoC** serves as the de facto border between **India** and **Pakistan** in the region of **Jammu and Kashmir**, and most cross-border operations are focused on this **740-km long** boundary.
 
• **Strategic Impact**: Beyond the immediate destruction of camps, such operations serve as a **psychological deterrent** and demonstrate **technological superiority** in the **South Asian** theater.

questions.question: Which national park was declared India’s 58th Tiger Reserve in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Madhav National Park, Madhya Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Madhav National Park**, located in the **Shivpuri** district of **Madhya Pradesh**, was officially designated as India’s **58th Tiger Reserve** in **March 2025**.
 
• The notification was issued by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** following the final approval from the **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA)**.
 
• This declaration makes **Madhya Pradesh** the state with the highest number of tiger reserves in India, bringing its total count to **8** (including Kanha, Bandhavgarh, Panna, Pench, Satpura, Sanjay-Dubri, and Veerangana Durgavati).
 
• The initiative is part of a broader conservation strategy to reintroduce and stabilize tiger populations in the **Gwalior-Chambal** region and create a functional wildlife corridor connecting **Ranthambore Tiger Reserve** in **Rajasthan** with **Kuno National Park** and **Madhav National Park**.
 
• Historically, **Madhav National Park** was the shooting reserve of the **Maharajas of Gwalior**; it was granted the status of a **National Park** in **1958**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Madhav National Park, Madhya Pradesh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project Tiger:**
 
 
• Launched on **April 1, 1973**, from **Jim Corbett National Park**, it is a centrally sponsored scheme aimed at ensuring a viable population of **Bengal Tigers** in their natural habitats.
 
• The project has expanded from an initial **9 reserves** to **58 reserves** as of **2025**, covering over **2%** of India's geographical area.
 
 
 
• **National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA):**
 
 
• The **NTCA** is a statutory body under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change**, constituted under the enabling provisions of the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**, as amended in **2006**.
 
• It provides statutory authority to **Project Tiger** and oversees the management and protection of tiger reserves across various states.
 
 
 
• **Tiger Census in India:**
 
 
• India conducts a nationwide **Tiger Census** every **four years** using the **M-STrIPES** (Monitoring System for Tigers - Intensive Protection and Ecological Status) application.
 
• According to the **2022 Tiger Census**, India is home to approximately **3,682 tigers**, which constitutes about **75%** of the global wild tiger population.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Madhav National Park:**
 
 
• The park is situated in the **Vindhyan Hills** and features a diverse ecosystem consisting of **dry deciduous forests** and flat grasslands.
 
• It is home to the **Sakhya Sagar** and **Madhav Sagar** lakes, which are designated **Ramsar Sites**, providing a crucial habitat for migratory birds and crocodiles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Status of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Ramgarh Vishdhari National Park** (Rajasthan) was notified as India's **52nd Tiger Reserve** in **May 2022**.
 
• **Orang National Park** (Assam) was declared a tiger reserve in **2016**, becoming the **49th** in the country.
 
• **Guru Ghasidas National Park** (Chhattisgarh) and **Tamor Pingla Wildlife Sanctuary** were combined to be declared the **56th Tiger Reserve** in late **2024**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Notification:**
 
 
• Being declared a **Tiger Reserve** allows the park to receive dedicated funding and specialized protection forces under **Project Tiger**, enhancing anti-poaching measures and habitat management.

questions.question: Apart from 30th January, on which other date is Martyrs’ Day observed in India to honour Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**23rd March**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Martyrs' Day**, also known as **Shaheed Diwas**, is observed on **23rd March** every year to pay homage to the great revolutionaries **Bhagat Singh**, **Shivaram Rajguru**, and **Sukhdev Thapar**.
 
• On this day in **1931**, these three young freedom fighters were hanged by the **British Government** in the **Lahore Central Jail**.
 
• They were executed for their involvement in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case**, specifically for the assassination of British police officer **John Saunders** in **1928** to avenge the death of **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
 
• Although the execution was originally scheduled for **24th March 1931**, the British authorities carried it out 11 hours early, on the evening of **23rd March**, due to the fear of a massive public uprising.
 
• The bodies of the three martyrs were secretly cremated by the authorities near the **Sutlej River** in **Ferozepur**, Punjab.
 
• While **30th January** is observed as Martyrs' Day to mark the assassination of **Mahatma Gandhi** in **1948**, **23rd March** is specifically dedicated to the sacrifice of these three revolutionaries. ***Hence, the correct answer is 23rd March.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhagat Singh and the HSRA:**
 
 
• **Bhagat Singh** was a charismatic Indian revolutionary who played a crucial role in the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**, which was founded in **1928** at **Feroz Shah Kotla**, Delhi.
 
• In **April 1929**, **Bhagat Singh** and **Batukeshwar Dutt** threw non-lethal bombs into the **Central Legislative Assembly** to protest against the **Public Safety Bill** and the **Trade Dispute Bill**.
 
• Their intent was not to kill but "to make the deaf hear," and they surrendered voluntarily to use the court trials as a platform to spread their revolutionary ideas.
 
 
 
• **Other Significant Dates in the Options:**
 
 
• **13th April:** This date marks the **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** that occurred in **1919** in Amritsar, where British troops under **General Dyer** fired on a peaceful gathering.
 
• **9th August:** This date is associated with the launch of the **Quit India Movement** in **1942** and the **Kakori Train Action (Conspiracy)** in **1925**.
 
• **15th March:** This day is observed as **World Consumer Rights Day** globally, but it does not hold a specific national Martyrs' Day status in India.
 
 
 
• **Other Martyrs' Days in India:**
 
 
• **21st October:** Observed as **Police Martyrs' Day** (Police Commemoration Day) to remember the policemen killed by Chinese troops at **Hot Springs** in Ladakh in **1959**.
 
• **17th November:** Observed in **Odisha** to commemorate the death anniversary of **Lala Lajpat Rai**, the "Lion of Punjab."
 
• **19th November:** The birthday of **Rani Lakshmibai** is often observed as Martyrs' Day in the region of **Jhansi** to honor those who fell in the **Rebellion of 1857**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legal Background:** The trio was tried under a special tribunal constituted by the **Viceroy Lord Irwin** through an ordinance, bypassing the regular court process to ensure a swift execution.
 
• **Legacy:** The slogan **"Inquilab Zindabad"** (Long Live the Revolution) was popularized by **Bhagat Singh** and became the war cry of the Indian independence movement.
 
• **National Tribute:** Every year, the Prime Minister and other leaders pay floral tributes at the **National Martyrs Memorial** located in **Hussainiwala** (Ferozepur district, Punjab), where the trio was cremated.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following Brazilian cities hosted the 17th BRICS Summit on 6–7 July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rio de Janeiro**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brazil** officially assumed the **Presidency** of the **BRICS** group for the year **2025**, succeeding **Russia**, which held the chairmanship in **2024**.
 
• The **17th BRICS Summit** is scheduled to be hosted in the city of **Rio de Janeiro** on **6–7 July 2025**.
 
• The summit in **Rio de Janeiro** represents the first major gathering of the expanded **BRICS+** bloc under **Brazilian** leadership, following the historic expansion that included **Egypt**, **Ethiopia**, **Iran**, and the **United Arab Emirates (UAE)**.
 
• The **Brazilian Chairmanship** has prioritized themes such as **global governance reform**, **sustainable development**, and **energy transition** as part of the **2025** agenda.
 
• The choice of **Rio de Janeiro**, a major cultural and economic hub, aligns with **Brazil's** strategy to showcase its international standing and its role in **South-South cooperation**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Rio de Janeiro.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolution of BRICS**:
 
 
• The acronym **BRIC** was first coined in **2001** by **Jim O'Neill** of **Goldman Sachs** to identify the fast-growing economies of **Brazil**, **Russia**, **India**, and **China**.
 
• The first formal summit took place in **Yekaterinburg**, **Russia**, in **June 2009**. **South Africa** was invited to join the group in **December 2010**, turning the acronym into **BRICS**.
 
 
 
• **Brasilia**:
 
 
• As the federal capital of **Brazil**, **Brasilia** has hosted several high-level diplomatic events, including the **11th BRICS Summit** in **November 2019**.
 
• It remains the center for administrative and legislative decisions but was not the primary host city for the **July 2025** summit.
 
 
 
• **Sao Paulo**:
 
 
• Known as the financial heart of **Brazil** and the most populous city in the **Southern Hemisphere**, **Sao Paulo** frequently hosts **BRICS Business Forums** and financial track meetings.
 
• It plays a vital role in **trade relations** and **foreign direct investment** within the bloc.
 
 
 
• **Manaus**:
 
 
• Located in the **Amazon** region, **Manaus** often serves as a venue for **BRICS** discussions related to **environmental policy**, **biodiversity**, and the **bio-economy**.
 
• It is a key location for **Brazil's** environmental diplomacy but does not serve as the main **2025** summit host.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **New Development Bank (NDB)**: Established during the **6th BRICS Summit** in **Fortaleza**, **Brazil** (**2014**), the **NDB** is headquartered in **Shanghai**, **China**. It provides funding for infrastructure and sustainable projects in **emerging markets**.
 
• **Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA)**: A framework established by **BRICS** nations to provide **liquidity support** and protection against global financial pressures, strengthening the **financial safety net** of member states.
 
• **Rotation Policy**: The **Chairmanship** of **BRICS** rotates annually among members according to the acronym. Following **Brazil** in **2025**, the presidency will move to **Russia** (based on the updated rotation including new members).
 
• **BRICS+ Expansion**: The **15th Summit** in **Johannesburg** (**2023**) led to the invitation of new members, significantly increasing the bloc's share of the **global GDP** and **world population**.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian banks increased the minimum balance requirement for new customers for the semi-urban segment branches to ₹25,000, compared to its earlier ₹5,000 levels from August 1, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ICICI Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ICICI Bank**, one of India's leading private sector lenders, has implemented a substantial revision in its **minimum balance requirements** for specific branch categories.
 
• For **new customers** opening accounts in **semi-urban** segment branches, the **Average Monthly Balance (AMB)** requirement has been increased to **₹25,000**.
 
• This marks a significant jump from the earlier requirement of **₹5,000**, representing a five-fold increase in the threshold for **semi-urban** areas.
 
• The revised policy is set to come into effect starting from **August 1, 2025**. ***Hence, the correct answer is ICICI Bank.***
 
• Such adjustments are often made by private banks to align with their **operational costs** and to target specific **customer segments** that maintain higher liquidity in their accounts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICICI Bank (Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India):**
 
 
• It is a prominent **Indian multinational bank** and financial services company headquartered in **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• The bank was originally promoted in **1955** by the **World Bank**, the Government of India, and representatives of Indian industry.
 
• The current **Managing Director** and **CEO** of the bank is **Sandeep Bakhshi**.
 
• It offers a wide range of banking products and financial services to corporate and retail customers through a variety of delivery channels and specialized subsidiaries.
 
 
 
• **Branch Classification in India:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** classifies bank branches based on population. **Semi-urban** branches are typically located in centers with a population of **10,000 to less than 1,00,000**.
 
• **Rural** centers have a population up to **9,999**, while **Urban** centers range from **1,00,000 to 9,99,999**, and **Metropolitan** centers have **10,00,000** and above.
 
 
 
• **Average Monthly Balance (AMB):**
 
 
• **AMB** is the minimum average balance a customer is required to maintain in their savings account over a month to avoid **non-maintenance charges**.
 
• It is calculated by adding the **closing balance** of each day in the month and dividing the total by the **number of days** in that month.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Public Sector Banks:**
 
 
• In contrast to private players like **ICICI Bank** or **HDFC Bank**, public sector banks like the **State Bank of India (SBI)** have largely moved away from **AMB** penalties.
 
• **SBI** waived the **Average Monthly Balance** requirement for all **Savings Bank Accounts** in **March 2020** to encourage **financial inclusion** and provide relief to its vast customer base.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Customers:**
 
 
• High **minimum balance** requirements can act as a barrier for low-income individuals in **semi-urban** areas, potentially shifting them toward **Public Sector Banks** or **Small Finance Banks**.
 
• Failure to maintain the required **₹25,000** after the **August 1, 2025** deadline will lead to **penal charges**, which vary based on the percentage of the shortfall.

questions.question: Which of the following missile systems did India test within a 24-hour window in July 2025, showcasing strategic deterrence capabilities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prithvi-II, Agni-I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India achieved a significant milestone in strategic deterrence by successfully testing the **Prithvi-II** and **Agni-I** missile systems within a narrow **24-hour window** in **July 2025**.
 
• These consecutive tests were conducted as part of the routine user training launches by the **Strategic Forces Command (SFC)** to validate the operational readiness and technical parameters of India's nuclear-capable arsenal.
 
• The launches took place from the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** at **Chandipur** and **APJ Abdul Kalam Island** off the coast of **Odisha**, demonstrating seamless coordination and logistical efficiency of the defense forces.
 
• The **Prithvi-II** test confirmed its high degree of precision and reliability for short-range targets, while the **Agni-I** test reinforced the strength of India's medium-range strike capabilities. ***Hence, the correct option is Prithvi-II, Agni-I.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prithvi-II Missile:**
 
 
• It is a **surface-to-surface short-range ballistic missile (SRBM)** developed by the **DRDO** under the **Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP)**.
 
• The missile is powered by **liquid propulsion twin engines** and has a strike range of approximately **350 km**.
 
• It is capable of carrying **500 kg to 1000 kg** of warheads and uses an advanced inertial guidance system with maneuvering trajectories to hit its target.
 
 
 
• **Agni-I Missile:**
 
 
• **Agni-I** is a **medium-range ballistic missile (MRBM)** that serves as a critical component of India's credible minimum deterrence.
 
• It utilizes a **single-stage solid-fuel engine**, which allows for quicker mobilization and launch compared to liquid-fueled systems.
 
• The missile has a range of **700 km to 1200 km** and is designed to be road-mobile, enhancing its survivability during conflict.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Forces Command (SFC):**
 
 
• Formed in **January 2003**, the **SFC** is part of India's **Nuclear Command Authority (NCA)**.
 
• It is responsible for the management and administration of the country's tactical and strategic nuclear weapons stockpile.
 
• The **SFC** ensures that the "no-first-use" policy of **India** is backed by a robust and ready delivery system.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Testing:**
 
 
• Testing multiple systems within **24 hours** signals to global observers the high level of **automation** and **readiness** of India's missile silos and mobile launchers.
 
• The data gathered from these tests in **2025** helps **DRDO** scientists refine guidance systems and re-entry technologies for future iterations like **Agni-Prime**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Integrated Test Range (ITR):** Located in **Odisha**, this facility provides the necessary infrastructure for performance evaluation of various missiles and rockets.
 
• **Nuclear Triad:** India possesses the capability to launch nuclear weapons from **land**, **air**, and **sea** (via **INS Arihant**), and these missile tests are essential for the land-based leg of the triad.
 
• **Other Missiles:** While **Agni-V** has an **intercontinental range (ICBM)** of over **5000 km**, and **BrahMos** is a **supersonic cruise missile**, they were not the specific systems tested in this particular **24-hour** window in **July 2025**.
</ul

questions.question: Haryana’s 2025 environmental plan aims to fully eliminate stubble burning by which target year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2030**__.

questions.question: What is the name of the submarine commissioned by India on January 15, 2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Navy** officially commissioned **INS Vagsheer** on **January 15, 2025**. This submarine represents the **sixth** and final vessel of the **Project-75** (P-75) **Kalvari-class**.
 
• The commissioning ceremony took place at the **Naval Dockyard** in **Mumbai**, marking a significant milestone in India's naval capabilities and domestic shipbuilding.
 
• **INS Vagsheer** was built by **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL)** in **Mumbai**, in technical collaboration with the **Naval Group** of **France**.
 
• The submarine is designed to operate in various naval theaters, capable of performing diverse missions such as **anti-surface warfare**, **anti-submarine warfare**, **intelligence gathering**, **mine laying**, and **area surveillance**.
 
• The naming of the submarine follows the naval tradition of resurrecting names of illustrious predecessors; it is named after the **Sand Fish**, a deadly deep-sea predator of the **Indian Ocean**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Project-75 and the Kalvari Class:**
 
 
• **Project-75** involved the construction of **six** **Scorpene-class** diesel-electric attack submarines.
 
• The first five submarines of this class already in active service are **INS Kalvari** (commissioned in **2017**), **INS Khanderi** (**2019**), **INS Karanj** (**2021**), **INS Vela** (**2021**), and **INS Vagir** (**2023**).
 
• These submarines are known for their advanced **stealth features**, including superior **acoustic absorption** techniques, low radiated noise levels, and a hydro-dynamically optimized shape.
 
 
 
• **Technical Specifications:**
 
 
• **INS Vagsheer** is equipped with **long-range guided torpedoes** and **tube-launched anti-ship missiles**, providing it with a lethal "punch" to strike targets both on the surface and underwater.
 
• It features the **Submarine Tactical Integrated Combat System (SUBTICS)**, which integrates all sensors and weapon systems for efficient combat management.
 
• The submarine can operate at high speeds and reach significant depths, making it difficult for enemy sensors to detect.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The original **INS Vagsheer** was a **Vela-class** (Soviet Foxtrot-class) submarine commissioned into the **Indian Navy** on **December 26, 1974**, and was decommissioned on **April 30, 1997**, after two decades of service.
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** The completion of the **Project-75** series is a major boost to the **"Make in India"** and **"Atmanirbhar Bharat"** (Self-reliant India) initiatives, showcasing India’s prowess in complex underwater engineering.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** With the commissioning of **INS Vagsheer**, the **Indian Navy** enhances its maritime security posture in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**, ensuring better protection of sea lines of communication and deterrent capabilities against regional threats.
 
• **Future Prospects:** Following the completion of **Project-75**, the Indian government is moving forward with **Project-75I**, which aims to build even more advanced submarines with **Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP)** systems to increase underwater endurance.

questions.question: The National Sports Governance Act, 2025, was enacted to address which of the following?

options.text: Challenges and impediments in the governance of sports bodies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Challenges and impediments in the governance of sports bodies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Sports Governance Act, 2025** was primarily enacted to create a comprehensive legal framework to tackle the deep-rooted **challenges and impediments** within the administration of sports in the **country**.
 
• It aims to bring about structural reforms in the **National Sports Federations (NSFs)** and the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)** to ensure they operate with **transparency, accountability, and professionalism**. ***Hence, the correct answer is option 4.***
 
• One of the primary objectives is to address the **lack of transparency** in the election processes and the **extended tenures** of office bearers that often lead to a monopoly over sports administration.
 
• The act provides a statutory basis for the **National Sports Development Code of India**, transforming it from a set of guidelines into a mandatory legal obligation for all recognized sports bodies.
 
• It focuses on removing **administrative bottlenecks** that have historically led to legal disputes, mismanagement of funds, and a lack of proper support for athletes at the **grassroots level**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Good Governance Norms**: 
 
 
• The act mandates the implementation of **age and tenure limits** for officials, typically restricting the **President** and other key members to a maximum of **12 years** or **three terms**.
 
• It emphasizes **gender representation**, requiring sports bodies to have a minimum percentage of **women** in their executive committees to promote inclusivity.
 
 
 
• **Athlete-Centric Approach**: 
 
 
• A significant feature is the mandatory inclusion of **Sportspersons of Outstanding Merit (SOM)** in the decision-making process, ensuring at least **25%** representation of athletes in the executive body.
 
• This ensures that the **features** of sports policies are designed with the direct input of those who have practical experience in the field.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight**: 
 
 
• The act proposes the establishment of an independent **Sports Regulatory Board** to monitor the compliance of federations with the established **governance standards**.
 
• It also brings sports bodies under the ambit of the **Right to Information (RTI) Act**, making their **financial data** and administrative decisions accessible to the public.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dispute Resolution**: The **National Sports Governance Act, 2025** introduces a specialized **Sports Arbitration Tribunal** to resolve internal conflicts and selection disputes swiftly, reducing the burden on the **judiciary**.
 
• **Financial Integrity**: It mandates regular **audits** by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** or government-approved auditors for federations receiving **grants** and subsidies from the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• **Anti-Doping and Ethics**: The act reinforces compliance with **World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)** and **National Anti-Doping Agency (NADA)** protocols, making the federations directly responsible for the **ethical conduct** of their members.
 
• **Global Alignment**: By streamlining governance, India aims to align its domestic sports law with the **Olympic Charter**, preventing potential suspensions of the **National Olympic Committee** by international bodies due to **government interference**.
</ul
